items.title: Researchers Hack Volkswagen Cars via Bluetooth to Spy on Conversations and Track GPS Locations
items.description: Bluetooth flaws in Volkswagen cars could expose private conversations, reveal GPS locations, and allow unauthorized control of cabin features. The findings highlight a lengthy patch rollout, with some vehicles remaining exposed roughly 16 months after the vulnerabilities became public. items.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra has found and exploited zero-day vulnerabilities affecting a popular mobile operating system and a widely hosted network service, according to the company’s latest system card. items.title: Cleverbridge Confirms Hackers Stole Customer Card Numbers and CVV Codes in a Major Data Breach
items.description: Cleverbridge confirmed that hackers copied payment card data from its e-commerce platform. The stolen information includes card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV or CVC security codes. Cleverbridge’s public update does not list those fields or say whether the same details were exposed for every affected customer. The company began notifying affected individuals on November 20, […] The post…

items.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
items.description: GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices, with some affected users reporting backdoors and reverse shells giving remote access to infected devices. [...]

items.title: VirusTotal’s New Ransomware Detection Catches Malware Missed by All 75 Antivirus Engines
items.description: VirusTotal has rolled out a ransomware detection update that checks whether suspicious files actually encrypt user documents during execution. The new checks caught a Python ransomware sample that recorded zero detections across 75 antivirus engines at the time of analysis, showing how behavior checks can expose threats that static scanning misses. The update spans VirusTotal […] The post…

items.description: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown. items.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
items.description: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions.
